newsitem.title: GERMANY: German govt ally attacks clumsy finance policy.
newsitem.headline: German govt ally attacks clumsy finance policy.

text.p: Otto Lambsdorff, honorary chairman of the government's Free Democratic (FDP) junior coalition partners, on Thursday accused Finance Minister Theo Waigel of clumsy handling of Germany's current budget problems.

While Lambsdorff, a former German economics minister, described Waigel's plan to revalue Bundesbank gold and currency reserves as legitimate, he said the timing of the announcement on the plan was poor.

"The presentation of the unfavourable (1997) tax estimate and the simultaneous assault on the council of the Bundesbank do not suggest a far-sighted and careful financial policy," Lambsdorff said in a statement.

Lambsdorff said that, contrary to what opposition figures had suggested, the profits from an upwards revaluation of bank reserves would not be placed into the current budget and could in no way be seen as a "creative" accounting measure to ensure maintenance of European monetary union economic criteria.

Opposition politicians earlier called for Waigel's resignation after the central bank on Wednesday rejected Bonn's plans to revalue its assets. The government said it would go ahead with the plan regardless.

Lambsdorff earlier this month criticised Waigel, of the Christian Social Union (CSU) party, for souring relations with his coalition partners the FDP for continuing to rule out tax rises to stop up budget holes.
The FDP has been vocal against any increases in tax.
